Welcome to Phakama

Who We Are.

Learn who we are, what we stand for and how we are working with communities across the Eastern Cape to strengthen accountability, promote development and build a better future for all.

Although Phakama will participate in democratic processes where communities mandate us to do so, our identity remains that of a civic movement committed to serving communities beyond election cycles.

Our Approach

How We
Work.

Lasting change happens when communities, government, traditional leaders, business and civil society work together around a shared vision for the future.

01

Community First

We listen before we act, ensuring that our work is informed by the real needs and aspirations of communities.

02

Partnership over Confrontation

We believe respectful engagement, collaboration and evidence-based advocacy produce more sustainable outcomes than conflict alone.

03

From Ideas to Action

We strive to move beyond identifying problems by building partnerships, supporting implementation and contributing to long-term solutions.

Current Priorities

What We're
Focused On.

🎓

Community Career Exhibition & Rural Development Dialogue

Preparing young people for brighter futures through education, career guidance and rural development dialogue in Mbashe Local Municipality.

🏦

Phakama Corporate Banking Institution (CBI)

Building community-owned financial solutions that promote savings, investment and economic empowerment.

🇿🇦

Community Safety & Rule of Law

Promoting lawful governance, effective law enforcement and safer communities through constructive civic engagement and advocacy.

🗳️

Local Government Election Readiness

Preparing to strengthen local democracy by promoting ethical leadership, active citizenship and community-centred representation in the 2026 Local Government Elections.

🤝

Strategic Partnerships & Organisational Growth

Building strong partnerships, strengthening organisational capacity and expanding Phakama’s provincial footprint to increase sustainable community impact.

Core Pillars

Our Blueprint
for Revival.

We approach governance and community development fundamentally differently. We measure success by jobs created, infrastructure built, and services delivered.

01

Economy & Jobs

Transforming agriculture, creating specialized economic zones, and driving targeted youth employment initiatives.

02

Dignified Services

Ensuring clean water, fixing failing healthcare, eradicating mud schools, and sustainable waste management.

03

Infrastructure

Prioritizing road maintenance, upgrading electrical grids, and accelerating dignified housing projects.

Our Future
Our Vision for the Eastern Cape
"We believe every community deserves accountable leadership, meaningful opportunities and the chance to shape its own future."

Together with citizens, partners and institutions, we are building an Eastern Cape where communities do not simply receive development — they help lead it.

    Strategic Timeline

    The Action
    Plan.

    A phased approach to building a formidable, self-sustaining provincial movement from the ground up.

    Phase One

    Establish.

    Laying the institutional foundation for a province-wide movement.

    Provincial Imbizo

    Gathering representatives from all districts to ratify the constitution and mandate.

    Governance Documents

    Drafting strict codes of conduct, accountability frameworks, and policy baselines.

    Leadership Identification

    Vetting and onboarding ward-level organizers and steering committee members.

    Phase Two

    Operate.

    Building the machinery that keeps the movement running across the province.

    Community Dialogues

    Hosting weekly town halls in targeted wards to identify immediate civic action targets.

    Political Education

    Training volunteers on constitutional rights, municipal budgeting, and accountability tools.

    Volunteer Networks

    Deploying structured teams for civic action, from clean-ups to service delivery monitoring.

    Phase Three

    Implement.

    Turning strategy into visible change on the ground through targeted execution.

    Direct Action

    Executing planned campaigns like road audits, infrastructure monitoring, and clinic assessments.

    Legal Interventions

    Using PAIA requests and court actions to force municipal compliance and transparency.

    Electoral Preparation

    Preparing the ground for direct electoral contestation where civic interventions hit political walls.
